07347
Understanding Macroeconomics
27
이채원
Macroeconomics is the study of the movement of the entire economy, and deals with macroeconomic variables such as national income, unemployment rate, inflation, economic growth, monetary policy, fiscal policy, international trade, and exchange rates. Understand and analyze the measurement method of national income including GDP and its components, and learn the driving force of economic growth and growth theory (Solow model, endogenous growth theory, etc.) to analyze economic growth. Analyze the impact of consumer spending and corporate investment decisions on the entire economy, learn about consumption functions and investment functions, understand the causes and types of unemployment, the causes of inflation and their economic impact, and analyze the correlation between unemployment and inflation using the Phillips curve, etc. Analyze the effects of the government's fiscal policy (taxes, government spending) and the central bank's monetary policy (interest rate adjustment, money supply) on the economy.

07135
Understanding financial statement analysis
23
허성준
Financial statement analysis is the process of analyzing a company's financial reports to evaluate the company's financial soundness, performance, and financial status. Financial statement analysis evaluates the financial soundness of a company. This allows you to assess a company's ability to meet its financial obligations now and over the long term and identify default risks. Financial statement analysis evaluates a company's profitability. This helps you understand how a company generates revenue, manages costs, and distributes profits. Financial statements show the status of a company's assets, liabilities, and equity. Through financial statement analysis, you can determine a company's capital structure, liquidity, and asset quality.

This course deals with the understanding of the concept and types of derivatives and the major derivatives. By dealing with risk hedging strategies using derivatives and investment strategies using derivatives, you can enhance your understanding of derivatives, and understand the valuation and investment strategies of derivatives.

이상호
Thefirm,while providing useful things to society, also generates harmful things such as pollution,industrialaccidents,and unemployment;andthere is tension between these two apsects of the firm.The society expects the firm to act appropriately,and the firm owners and managers must conform to such expectations.However, the expectation also causes friction between the society and managers.Corporate Social Responsibility(CSR)deals with how firms canbalance thedemands of its stockholders to maximize profits,andthe demandofthesociety forsustainable development and maximizing thesocial welfare.Thepublic demand for CSRIs rising so that society is no longer be satisfied with the fiscal and growthresponsibility of the past,but rather demand a much more complex behaviorand goals. 04297
Econometric Practice
The purpose of this subject is to learn the ability to handle the real data using the Econometrics methods. We need to analyze the collected data from society to learn the economic phenomena since it is almost impossible to expertiment the economic phenomena in closed lab. In this class, students learn to how to deal with data using econometrics methods using real life data. Students learn to analyze and interpret the data analysis results. Examples of analyses are the effects of Dow Jones index to KOSPI in financial economics, relationships between comsumption and income, output and money in macroeconomics, effects of age, education on income in labor economics, relationship of salary of pitcher and his performance in sports, and relationship of advertisement expenditure and sales in marketing. Students learn how to deal with the problems with data analyses such as heteroskedasticity and autocorrelation of error terms.
02395
International Finance
This course is the macroeconomic component of international economics. The course looks at how exchange rates are determined, how governments can set or influence the exchange rates, and how domestic macroeconomic policies work in the open economy. Contents include exchange rate theory, international monetary theory, international balance of payments and adjustments, and international capital mobility.

07256
Behavioral and Experimental Economics
42
This course will be an introduction to behavioral economics and experimental method, and some of the major topics that have been addressed. Behavioral economics extends economic principles by acknowledging that our decisions are affected by social and psychological influences, as well as rational calculations of benefits and costs. Experimental methods allow us to control economic institutions, information, policies, and other important variables, both in the laboratory and in the field. Through experiments, we can test the validity of economic theories, detect departures from those theories, and identify patterns of individual behavior useful for building new theories.
07255
Environmental Economics
41
This module, Environmental Economics, aims to provide balanced and rigorous training in modern theories and techniques for understanding topics related to the environment and the ecosystem. The module will utilize economic analysis and incorporate real-world examples. The topics covered in this module include: basic economic analyses, welfare economics, pollution control and management, international environmental cooperation, renewable resource management, climate change, and sustainable development.

The best way to learn environmental economics is by applying economic analysis to real-world examples. To facilitate this, we will extensively use classroom experiments, quizzes, and group projects. These activities will help students apply theoretical concepts to practical situations, enhancing their understanding and engagement with the material.

DIY Interior Design Utilizing Online Platform
신수영
Do-it-yourself (DIY) interior design or ‘self-interior design’, is defined as the remodeling of interior spaces by consumers without expert help, usually their homes. As the quality of life can be improved and one's own lifestyle and personality can be expressed at a low cost, DIY interior design is expanding from small-scale styling such as furniture, accessories, and fabrics to large-scale construction such as replacement of finishing materials. In this lecture, definition, design process, space modeling using 3D programs, online platform utilization and construction method of small space DIY interior design for university students and graduates will be discussed so that students can cultivate insight in interior design and raise spatial problem-solving ability to change their surroundings.

방주원
This introductory course for first-year spatial design majors focuses on building a fundamental understanding of graphic design. Students develop visual perception and design principles to support the transition from two-dimensional graphics to spatial applications.Through practical training in typography and layout systems, the course enhances symbolic and expressive design skills. It lays the groundwork for integrating visual communication into spatial design practices.
07101
Spatial Design Foundation
김나연
This course serves as an introductory major course in Spatial Design, offering fundamental practical experience in English.

The primary objective of this course is to comprehensively understand various spatial environments where life occurs and to enhance the necessary perspectives, theoretical knowledge, and spatial design expression skills needed to create them. We aim to broaden our perspective on how we perceive spatial environments in our daily lives, foster creative thinking, interdisciplinary abilities, and expressive skills to create improved spaces.

Throughout this course, students will practice exercises that involve expressing spaces using architectural elements, with the goal of developing perceptual and creative potential in relation to spaces. Students will gain experience in the basic architectural language of form required to create spaces accommodating human behavior, analyze spatial meanings, and cultivate spatial expression abilities during the design process. Additionally, the course aims to enhance conceptual idea development, visual communication skills, and provide fundamental practice in spatial design, ultimately contributing to a broader understanding of architecture and interior design as a whole.

● to observe and gain an understanding of the physical characteristics of the spatial environments in which we reside
● to understand architects’ philosophy, design concepts, and spatial drawings through the examination of global architectural works
● to understand spatial scale and design elements while acquiring the skills necessary for architectural representation techniques and 3D model making (including sketching, drawing, diagrams, photography, collage, 3D study models, etc.).
● to foster the design development of spatial concept ideas and enhance visual communication skills
● to Acquire knowledge of spatial design methods, fundamental components, and the overall design process.

Environmental Psychology and Neuroarchitecture
8
노태린

Through this process, students will acquire expertise in consumer-centered spatial design and cultivate practical design capabilities that respond to contemporary social demands.

07553
The Modern History of Korean Popular Culture
“The Modern History of Popular Culture in Korea” is a liberal arts course that explores the historical trajectory of Korean popular culture from the Japanese Colonial Period to the present. Rather than focusing on specific genres or content, it takes a broad approach, analyzing how popular culture has formed and evolved in relation to Korea’s political, economic, and social developments. Covering key periods—from the Japanese colonial rule to national liberation, the Korean War, industrialization, democratization, and the rise of the Korean Wave (Hallyu)—the course examines how popular culture has changed alongside broader societal shifts. Special attention is given to how culture intersects with issues of nationhood, class, locality, and gender, revealing the complex interplay between historical forces and cultural expression.
 Drawing on a wide range of sources—including historical records, audiovisual materials, literary texts, and cultural criticism—the course uses historical methodology to examine the production, circulation, and reception of popular culture. It challenges the view of the "mass" as passive consumers, highlighting their role as active producers and interpreters of culture shaped by their time. Through theoretical and historical analysis, students will gain a nuanced understanding of the relationships between culture and politics, structure and agency, and tradition and modernity. Ultimately, the course equips students with critical tools to analyze cultural phenomena within their historical contexts and to understand the shaping power of popular culture in modern Korean society.

07419
Principles of Economics
이종인
The Principles of Economics course is a foundational subject designed to introduce students to the basic concepts and principles of economics. This course aims to help students understand how economic systems operate and the processes involved in economic decision-making. It covers essential economic theories and provides students with the fundamental knowledge needed to analyze and resolve economic issues. 
The course begins by explaining the basic concepts of economics and how economic decisions impact society and individuals. Students learn about the importance of choice and the concept of opportunity cost in situations where resources are limited. Additionally, the course explores the interaction of supply and demand to understand how market equilibrium is achieved.
Students also examine the necessity of competition policy and regulation, and learn about the government's role in addressing market failures. The course further delves into the causes of economic growth and the cycles of economic fluctuation. It also covers the functions of money and the principles of money supply.

In this course, students learn theories related to establishing product, distribution, price, sales, and promotion strategies in a continuously changing market environment, discuss how to directly implement it, and analyze cases.

07327
ESG Management
손호철
The ESG Management course focuses on sustainable management and responsible business operations from the perspectives of Environment, Social, and Governance. It is designed to teach students how to strategically integrate ESG elements to achieve long-term success and sustainability for businesses. This course educates students on how companies can implement responsible management practices across environmental, social, and governance dimensions, thereby developing their ability to establish sustainable business strategies.
Students will gain an understanding of ESG concepts and their importance, learning how to evaluate a company's sustainability and social responsibility. The course emphasizes how companies can integrate ESG factors strategically to achieve long-term success and sustainability. Additionally, it highlights the significance of ethical management and transparent governance, and provides practical methods for implementing these principles. Students will also acquire skills to effectively report ESG performance and communicate with stakeholders. This course plays a crucial role in equipping students with the competencies needed to understand and apply ESG-related issues in modern business environments.

07523
Organization management
조진욱
Organizational Management is a course that comprehensively addresses the key elements necessary for effective organizational operation, including organizational structure, management principles, human resources and leadership, motivation, and change management. The main topics covered are the development of organizational theories (classical and modern), organizational structure and design, leadership and decision-making, performance management and evaluation, conflict management and organizational culture, as well as organizational change and innovation management.

The course is designed not only around theoretical lectures but also through the analysis of real corporate cases, including both successful and failed organizational management practices. In particular, it emphasizes discussion and case-based learning that leverage the professional backgrounds of adult learners, so that each student can connect their own organizational experiences to the classroom activities. Through this process, learners are expected not only to understand the foundational theories of organizational operation but also to critically analyze problems that arise in real workplaces and propose effective solutions.
06942
Start-up Business

It also develops the ability to discover and develop new ideas for entrepreneurial opportunities.

지호선

Focusing on creative problem-solving and real-world entrepreneurial experience, the course provides students with comprehensive skills and knowledge required to address community issues and generate economic value. Students will understand the characteristics and needs of their local communities and use this understanding to develop practical and innovative business ideas. They will engage in hands-on projects through teamwork and collaboration, gaining the planning, execution, and evaluation skills necessary for the entrepreneurial process.

Capstone Design-Sustainable management 1
This course is designed to develop students' ability to apply sustainable management principles to practical business models. It focuses on understanding the concepts of Sustainability Management and learning how to effectively implement these principles in real business environments. Students will develop comprehensive and innovative solutions by considering environmental, social, and economic aspects of sustainability, and will cultivate the skills necessary to design business models based on these solutions. The course also teaches students how to measure and evaluate the performance of sustainable management practices, enabling them to assess the success of their business models. Additionally, students will learn presentation skills to effectively communicate the results of their team projects and receive feedback through their presentations.

International Studies
04655
Introduction to International Relations
김준석
This course introduces students to major issues of international relations. The course deals with such topics as international relations theory, international security, international political economy, international human rights, and culture and international relations.
04656
Introduction to International Trade
윤미경
This course introduces students to major issues of international trade. Such topics as international trade theory and trade laws, and other various trade-related issues will be deal with.
04745
Policymaking in the European Union
베네딕트드도미닉
This course considers European regional integration trends, problems, progress and prospects of European policy-making.  It encourages a critical study of the EU institutional structure and policies as a means of facilitating European integration in a global context.  Policy focus areas correspond to the three pillars of the Maastricht Treaty.  EU intervention in South-east Europe and the Middle East is used to illustrate the impact of European integration on the peripheral European and Mediterranean regional political environment.  Over the next five years the European Union must overcome its biggest challenges since it was founded.  These challenges include 1) enlargement, 2) institutional reform, 3) safeguarding and improving EU competitiveness, and 4) the European Union’s global role as a power alongside the USA and Asia.  All four are interconnected and the events since 11 September have highlighted more than ever the need to turn the European Union into a global player.  In the major enlargement and reform process ahead, the objective is to create a strong, expanded European Union which is fully prepared to shoulder its political responsibilities on the world stage.  This course will highlight the policy making steps taken to meet these challenges.
04199
Theories and Realities of Economic Integration
Regionalism is a widespread phenomenon that occurs in almost every part of the world. About 140 regional preferential trading arrangements are in force at present.  Economic integration is not just an rational move to enhance economic efficiency by combining national markets on a regional scale, but a strategic and political move to promote national security, to enhance bargaining leverage in the multilateral negotiations, as well as to cultivate domestic political support. It requires  both removing border barriers and harmonizing domestic regulations. In this sense economic integration is both political and economic action.
05716
International Relations and Western Political Thought
This course aims to acquaint students with the works of Western political thinkers on international relations. Texts of such thinkers as Thucydides, Machiavelli, Hobbes, Grotius, Locke, Kant, Marx, Carl Schmitt would be intensively dealt with. Students who take this course are expected to get the chance to better understand the nature of international relations and also to think more deeply about its future prospect.

07253
Understanding International Disputes
이동은
his course aims to deeply explore the patterns, characteristics, and impacts of contemporary international conflicts, while studying various approaches to conflict resolution and peacebuilding through historical case studies. To achieve this, the course will analyze various international conflicts, including not only hot wars such as the war between Russia and Ukraine and the armed conflict between Israel and Hamas, but also the technological hegemony war between the U.S. and China and the discussions of a new Cold War. By integrating perspectives from international politics, international law, and world history, the course provides an academic foundation for a comprehensive understanding of international conflicts. Beyond acquiring theoretical knowledge, the course will foster analytical thinking and problem-solving skills in real-world international issues, contributing to the foundation for students to grow into global leaders.

It analyzes the linkages between development cooperation and trade rules – such as those under the World Trade Organization (WTO), free trade agreements (FTAs), and especially the newly arising issue related to industrial subsidies and intellectual property rights. Based on both theoretical treatment and case studies, students will develop a practical thinking and problem solving abilities required in the international development cooperation field.

글로벌학생지원팀
07204
College Korean1
4/2
When learning a new language, the most fundamental aspect is often mastering its grammatical rules. From the perspectives of communication approaches or holistic language approaches, grammar may be considered less important compared to other language elements like vocabulary or sentences. However, even if one possesses a rich vocabulary and knows various expressions, lacking knowledge of grammar can hinder the ability to construct accurate sentences, leading to difficulties in effective communication. Moreover, for learners of Korean, there is a strong demand for proficiency in the expressive aspect, and it is not an exaggeration to say that the foundation of language production begins with precise knowledge of grammar. In this course, based on a gradual understanding of the Korean grammar system, we aim to enhance the ability to generate accurate Korean sentences and promote metacognitive improvement, allowing learners to diagnose their own Korean grammar proficiency.
07205
College Korean2
Even without knowing grammar, there is a saying that one can start communicating to some extent as long as they know vocabulary, highlighting the significance of vocabulary in foreign language learning. The exclusion of the vocabulary section in the Test of Proficiency in Korean (TOPIK) does not diminish the importance of vocabulary; rather, it signifies that vocabulary is foundational in listening, reading, and writing across all areas. Departing from the past perspective that viewed vocabulary as a disorderly and infinite set that must be memorized without any order, we need to approach vocabulary with its own set of rules and apply them to vocabulary learning. In this course, based on a gradual understanding of the Korean vocabulary system, we aim to enhance the ability to use Korean vocabulary accurately and appropriately, while also fostering metacognitive improvement for learners to assess their own Korean vocabulary proficiency.
07206
College Korean3
In natural teaching methods, the initiation of foreign language learning has long been seen as starting with ‘listening’, a principle that continues to be accepted as a fundamental aspect of both native and foreign language acquisition. Individuals aspiring to learn Korean often have a strong desire to express themselves in Korean. However, since the use of language skills in human daily life places a significant emphasis on ‘listening’, accounting for about half of language use, it is essential to prioritize the improvement of listening skills. In this course, through various Korean listening exercises and practical, complex tasks, we aim to enhance accurate and fluent Korean listening abilities. Additionally, the course seeks to foster metacognitive improvement, allowing learners to assess their own Korean listening proficiency.
07207
College Korean4
Undoubtedly, the language skill most prioritized for academic pursuits is 'reading,' and this applies equally to international students studying abroad. To continue one's studies using various Korean academic textbooks and materials, securing proficiency in Korean reading is essential. However, 'reading' skills go beyond simply deciphering characters; they involve the ability to analyze, interpret, and creatively reconstruct content for comprehension. Specialized education is required to enhance these skills when working with Korean textual material. In this course, through various Korean reading exercises and practical, complex tasks, we aim to improve accurate and fluent Korean reading abilities. Additionally, the course seeks to foster metacognitive improvement, allowing learners to assess their own Korean reading proficiency.
07240
Academic Korean1
When learning a new language, the most fundamental aspect is understanding its rule system, namely, its grammar. This course aims to provide an advanced understanding of Korean grammar, building upon basic grammar knowledge to teach more complex and sophisticated sentence structures. The goal is to enable students to use Korean more naturally and fluently. Furthermore, through various grammatical diagnostic tools and feedback, the course promotes the development of students' metacognitive abilities to self-assess their Korean grammar skills.
07241
Academic Korean2
Vocabulary is a crucial element in learning a foreign language, playing a key role in determining communicative competence. This course aims to go beyond basic vocabulary learning, enhancing the accuracy and fluency of expression by using more advanced and diverse vocabulary. The course provides an in-depth understanding of the Korean vocabulary system, enabling students to learn complex words and idioms. Additionally, it cultivates the ability to select and use appropriate vocabulary in various contexts, ensuring effective communication not only in daily life but also in academic and professional settings. Furthermore, the course promotes the development of metacognitive skills, allowing students to self-assess their Korean vocabulary proficiency.
07242
Academic Korean3
Listening skills are a crucial element in foreign language learning, serving as the foundation for effective communication. This course aims to enhance students' listening abilities by utilizing advanced Korean listening materials beyond the basic level. The course focuses on improving accurate and fluent Korean listening skills through various listening exercises and practical, complex task performance. Additionally, it promotes the development of metacognitive skills that enable students to self-assess their Korean listening proficiency.
07243
Academic Korean4
Reading skills are the most crucial area for academic success, and this is equally true for international students. To continue their studies using various Korean-language textbooks and materials, acquiring proficient Korean reading skills is essential. The reading skills required at the university level go beyond simply reading text; they include the ability to analyze, interpret, and creatively reconstitute the material. Therefore, specialized education is necessary to improve these skills using Korean textual content. This course aims to enhance accurate and fluent Korean reading skills through various reading exercises and complex, practical tasks. Additionally, it promotes the development of metacognitive skills that enable students to self-assess their Korean reading proficiency.

03133
Discrete Mathematics
This course is designed to provide a rigorous foundation in logic and elementary discrete mathematics to students of mathematics and computer science. The emphasis is on logic and its application; the remaining mathematical topics are approached as a sequence of extensions to the predicate calculus. Topics from logic include textual substitution, Boolean expressions, modeling English propositions, and propositional and predicate calculi. Additional mathematical topics include elements of set theory, induction, relations and functions, and elements of number theory.
03151
Computer Architectures
이정현
This course examines the organization of computer and processor architectures. Instruction set design alternatives, processor implementation memory system hierarchy, and I/O systems are the main topics of study. The levels of abstraction in compute hardware are examined in theory and practice. The classic components of a computer system including CPU control and data path, ALU, memory, and input/output are covered, with supporting case studies in design and simulation. The use of a register transfer language is examined. Hardwired control and micro-programming control are examined in support or the implementation of a machine language. A design project ties together machine organization, assembly language programming, and logic and desing fundamentals. In addition to traditional architectures, high performance computing is considered, including CISC/RISC studies, pipelined architectures, and parallel processors.

University Prep Physics2
2/1
Physics is deeply related to differential equations. To understand how to solve various differential equations in physics, knowledge of matrices and complex numbers, let alone differentiation and integration, is indispensable. Through this course, students will be equipped with basic knowledge of matrices and complex numbers, which will help students learn physics major courses like classical mechanics, quantum mechanics, and so on. In addition, probability is an extremely important concept to understand quantum mechanics. In this course, students are asked to solve various problems after the lecturer explains important contents, to elicit students' understanding. The assessment will be given as pass or fail.

Object-oriented programming

07583
Database for Healthcare
This course provides a systematic introduction to relational database (RDB) theory and SQL programming within the context of healthcare and biomedical informatics. The first half of the course covers foundational concepts including data modeling, Entity-Relationship (ER) diagram design, normalization, and relational algebra, with practical examples drawn from real-world healthcare schemas aligned with medical informatics standards such as HL7 and ICD. The second half focuses on hands-on SQL practice using DBMS encompassing DDL, DML, complex JOIN operations, subqueries, and aggregate functions applied to biomedical datasets. In the final module, students work with de-identified clinical data to perform SQL-based data extraction and transformation, culminating in a pipeline exercise that feeds structured datasets into AI/ML models — bridging foundational database skills with applied AI literacy. This course is designed to equip students with the competencies required for industry-standard SQL certifications (e.g., SQLD) and to establish a rigorous data foundation for advanced coursework in biomedical AI implementation.

06260
Theoryofindividual fundamental rights
This course is an invitation to study of the theoryofindividual fundamental rights with the general constitutional theory. This course helps understanding of constitutional cases to individual fundamental rights. This course aims to provide students with opportunities to develop Basic theoryofthefundamentalrights and theoryofindividual fundamental rights for human rights protection. Our aim is to understand the meaning, character and the function of fundamental rights. At first we will investigate the nature, concept and function of individual fundamental rights in constitutional law. And we are concerned with analysing the characters and methods of the constitutional interpretation to individual fundamental rights. Thereafter we will deal with many issues relating to the essence and the system of individual fundamental rights with the conception of widening and deepening our understanding of the fundamental rights upon the Constitution, for example; what are the conditions of limitation on individual fundamental rights, human dignity and worth, equal protection before the law, civil liberties, political freedoms, procedural constitutional rights and social rights etc. We investigate the meanings, contents, and possibillities and limits of the restrictions on the individual rights of liberty through the critical review of the leading cases or the recent important decisions of the Constitutional Court.

양현
In modern capitalist society, people make their lives by working. While work is a process through which human beings make their own identity and give meanings to their lives, people may have to work for survival and are exposed to the harmful environment. Labor laws specify workers’ rights institutionally, but these rights are not fully guaranteed in their work due to the problems of the labor law itself and various conditions at their work place. In particular, college students who earn their income through part-time labor often do not know the rights in their jobs well. In this subject, we learn what the social, legal and institutional rights of workers are, and how these rights are linked to the human right issues in society as a whole.
박채은
03848
Gender and Culture in the Contemporary society
고윤경
유화정
06766
Cultural understanding of modern Korean society
김성윤
The age we live in today is the age of culture. Culture has become an essential keyword for understanding modern society. Culture, broadly defined, can be said to be the totality of the lifestyles of members of society. Modern Korean society has changed at an amazingly fast pace since the second half of the 20th century. The dynamics of changes in modern Korean society are particularly well-represented at the cultural level. As the social change that took more than 150 years to achieve in the developed countries of the West took less than 50 years in Korea, modern Korean society is culturally very complex, characterized by “simultaneity of asynchronousness” in which premodern-modern-postmodernity is mixed together.
  This course aims to examine various aspects of modern Korean society formed in the process of rapid modern change from a viewpoint of cultural sociology. Cultural sociology is a branch of sociology that studies how culture interacts with social institutions or structures that regulate human behavior in a society. The outline of the lecture contents of this course is as follows. First, we examine classical and modern sociological theories and debates about how culture is created, maintained, and reproduced in society. Next, we analyze various topics related to class, gender, generation, family, popular culture, leisure, body, consumption, food, politics, communication, technology, globalization, and multiculturalism in modern Korean society from a cultural sociological perspective, Furthermore, this course is going to grasp the universality and uniqueness of Korean social and culture through a comparative cultural approach that compares the social culture of Korea with that of China and Japan, which are neighboring countries.   
   Through the reading of sociological culture as described above, this course is expected to enable students to better understand the nature and working principle of modern Korean society, and to greatly develop cultural reflection and literacy skills on Korean society.

05845
Population & Society
This course will serve as a general introduction to the field of population studies. At the same time, we will examine a number of topics lying at the intersection of demography and sociology. This course is divided into two parts. In the first part, you will learn basic concepts and measures of demography, perspectives, and demographic trends. It includes overview of mortality, fertility, and migration that are essential demographic topics. The second part covers how population phenomena are intertwined with numerous social issues, such as poverty and inequality, family, labor market, globalization, urbanization, and social policy. In this course, we will focus on a variety of developmental issues in different countries (especially developing world) as well as in Korean context. For this reason, students need to keep a global perspective in reading, thinking, and conducting their research for this course.

06213
Industrial Microbiology
김형권
Microbiology is a field of life sciences that studies life as a microorganism. Early microbiology mainly dealt with pathogens of humans, animals, and grains, and later food microbiology related to food fermentation and storage problems was also studied. Today, it is an important position as a basic science to identify life phenomena. In particular, industrial microbiology uses microorganisms to produce antibiotics, enzymes, vitamins, alcohols, organic acids, and fuel materials, and to educate the screening, improvement and cultivation of industrially useful microbial strains. In addition, it uses genetic engineering technology to educate the technology of mass production of desired biomaterials.

06389
Brain and Cognition
신경순
Brain science is a natural science that researches human cognition quantitatively objectively and scientifically through various methods such as experiments, computer simulation etc. In the 1980s, the development of brain imaging techniques led to neuroscientific attempts to explore the problems of the mind from a physical standpoint, and as a result, the view that the study of the mind in humans should not be separated from brain research has become mainstream. 
  Psychology is known to explore the information processing, such as attention, perception, memory, learning, emotion, language and thought, which are the processes of the mind by the human brain and to apply the results. The study of this not only calls for observation, experimentation and rational reasoning, but also for a deep understanding of human beings. 
  The convergence between human brain and cognition by the action of mind is an important topic in both brain science and psychology. In particular, the ultimate goal of future convergence between science and technology is to promote human performance in various situations based on the development of hardware that has been achieved so far, and this is the core of the 4th Industrial Revolution. National Science Foundation emphasized that future science and technology should converge, integrate, teach, study and develop applications from the early stages of nano, bio, info and cogno. Bio and Cogno, or bio-science and cognitive science, are intended to be combined and connected. It is time to prepare for the 4th industrial revolution that requires students to take a convergent approach between psychology that concerns the essence of the human mind and brain science that analyzes the phenomenon of the brain in which the human mind is located. In this lecture, students can learn the structure and function of the human brain, which is a complex structure, deal with cognitive system, understand the human mind, examine  cognitive disorders, and expand their understanding of humans.

05605
Preliminary Parent Education
문혁준
Humans are born lethargic and grow depending on others' affection and help. It is the parents that provide such affection and help. Parent's role in such process can have a significant impact in child's physical, emotional, social, and cognitive development. In this sense, parental role is very important. The fact that young generations today are skeptical about this parental role, which requires parents to withstand much costs, is also the factor in lowering the birth rate of Korea. Birth rate drop does not only end simply by an individual not having a baby, but lead to the serious problem of bringing population issues to the society and nation. Meanwhile, parental roles in the modern society are very complex and difficult, compared to those in the past. Therefore, Preliminary Parent Education course aims to establish parenthood and basic ideas about parental roles, and will go over many educational activities that are necessary for maintaining a desirable parental role and parent-child relationship.
  We propose the Preliminary Parent Education course to become Catholic University's liberal arts program. This course aims to achieve the following course goals;
1) Prepares parenthood.
2) Acknowledges the necessity of parent education. 
3) Study the desirable parental roles according to child development phases.
4) Learn parent education programs that help improve parent-child relationships.
5) Understand problems of child abuse and preventive measures. 
6) Introduce that is currently implemented childbirth encouragement policy and experience the social atmosphere where child rearing is done not only in a parental responsibility, but in a national responsibility.
  This course includes lectures, watch videos, and student discussions. Especially, diverse topics that are shown in numerous social issues that reflect parenthood, or a desirable parental role, will be dealt with during student discussions. This procedure will emphasize the concept of 'parent' and 'parenthood' to the students. 
  Through this course, students will be able to possess positive thoughts about child birth and rearing, improve future potential parent-child relationships, and contribute to constructing a healthy family and society by preventing many problems that might occur during child rearing.

Pharmacy
06782
Pharmaceutical Basic Chemistry 2
권성윤
This course lectures on the basics of chemistry essential for understanding and manufacturing the properties of drugs. Modern chemistry consists of deriving and predicting macroscopic properties such as reaction heat, reaction speed, and equilibrium constant based on microscopic content understanding such as the electronic structure of atoms and molecules. Therefore, learning the basics of quantum mechanics and quantum chemistry to understand the electronic structure of atoms and molecules, and learning thermodynamics, thermochemistry, and reaction kinetics to systematically understand chemical reactions. It helps to comprehensively understand the properties of drugs through learning about acid base and redox reactions, which are representative chemical reactions closely related to real life.

Main topics include the concept of numerical computation by using computers, root finding, interpolation, approximation, and numerical integration/differentiation.

We study methods of numerical representation of problems in mathematics/science, mainly relating to linear algebra, and of numerical approach to solving those problems. Main topics include the concept of numerical computation by using computers, numerical solutions of systems of linear equations, numerical methods of solving differential equations.

Physical Pharmacy 1
강희은, 강한창

Based on the book 'Martin‘s Physical Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences', the course will cover states of matter, thermodynamics, physical properties of molecules, nonelectrolytes, electrolyte solutions, ionic equilibria, buffered and isotonic solutions, solubility and distribution phenomenon, and complexation and protein binding.

06746
Pharmaceutics Ⅱ
강내원
Pharmaceutics deals with principles and techniques of various dosage forms to deliver drugs to target sites effectively, safely, and reproducibly. All pharmaceutical products are formulated to specific dosage forms for drugs to be effectively delivered to patients. Different dosage forms require different pharmaceutical technologies and usually present different technical challenges for formulation development. This course covers the second half of comprehensive understanding and preparation for a variety of innovative delivery systems as well as conventional dosage forms.

Energy & Environmental Engineering
06290
Humanity and the environment
송규용
This curriculum examines the various environmental problems facing humanity. Explore ways to solve this.
The environment affects human activities. Human activities also have a direct or indirect impact on the environment.
Various factors, such as industrialization, advances in science and technology, and population growth, accelerate the pollution of the global environment. This threatens the survival of life, including humanity.
This curriculum seeks to understand how sustainable development can meet the needs of the present generation while not compromising the needs of the next generation. Learn how to deal with environmental issues by exploring the various conditions for doing this

water supply engineering
김영노

Students will understand the physico-chemical mechanisms of standard water treatment processes, including coagulation/flocculation, sedimentation, filtration, and disinfection. Additionally, the course explores advanced water treatment technologies for removing emerging micro-pollutants and examines recent domestic and international drinking water quality standards.

Numerical analysis for engineers
The actual energy and environment model are explained by a numerical analysis, which inputs a number of variables directly involved in the process and embodies the real process by obtaining output data.
06649
Energy balance and thermodynamics
This course covers the core theories and practical applications of mass and energy balances, and chemical engineering thermodynamics, which are essential for designing and optimizing energy and environmental processes. Students will learn to quantitatively analyze material and energy flows in various energy conversion systems and chemical reaction processes. Based on the first and second laws of thermodynamics, the curriculum explores equations of state, vapor-liquid equilibrium (VLE), and chemical reaction equilibrium. The course emphasizes engineering design capabilities to evaluate the efficiency of heat engines, refrigeration cycles, and power generation systems. As a senior-level advanced course, it aims to cultivate practical energy and environmental experts capable of leading energy efficiency processes in the era of carbon neutrality.

In addition, as our department changed its name to Department of Energy and Environmental Engineering from the spring semester of 2021, freshmen are increasingly curious about their career paths and research. Through this class, freshmen will be provided information with research and career paths in the fields of environmental engineering (water, air, soil, ect.) and energy (fossil fuel, renewable energy, ect.), which are the core subjects of the Department of Energy and Environmental Engineering.

Waste Treatment Engineering

Students will study the generation and physicochemical characteristics of municipal and hazardous wastes, alongside core waste management principles: reduction, reuse, and recycling. The curriculum emphasizes the design principles of physical pre-treatment (shredding, separation), thermal treatment (incineration, pyrolysis), and landfill engineering. Furthermore, by learning waste-to-energy technologies and environmental regulations, students will cultivate comprehensive capabilities as environmental engineers to solve practical waste problems and lead a carbon-neutral society.

06185
High-level English acquisition through a study of American English metaphors
김은주
This course aims to provide the students with a deep understanding of American culture and the acquisition of high-level vocabulary and speaking and writing practices of English through an in-depth study of a wide range of metaphor expressions in American English. The theoretical foundation for this course is the 'conceptual metaphor theory' in cognitive linguistics. This course is an integrated content-skill balanced course in English. The course features lectures on the metaphor theory and metaphor expressions in American English. Each lecture will be followed by the writing assignment and the speaking practices by the students. There will be a final presentation requirement.

예술미디어융합학과
07435
Media Technology and Culture
This subject explores the impact of developments in media technology on culture and society. From the early printing press to the latest technologies such as digital platforms, artificial intelligence (AI), and virtual reality (VR), we analyze how changes in various media technologies have changed cultural expressions and communication methods. Students can develop the ability to critically understand the interaction between media and technology and actively interpret the media environment of modern society.
07605
AX Character Desgin
길선영
The AX Character Design course guides students through the full pipeline of AI-driven creative production — from foundational concepts and prompt engineering to the generation of deployable outputs — developing both problem-solving capacity and practical fluency with AI tools. Students develop original character IPs through hands-on creation, gaining a working understanding of intellectual property frameworks, AI application strategies, and the pathway from concept to live service. Through this process, they acquire the core literacy needed to navigate the artistic and technical dimensions of AI-assisted creativity, culminating in a real-world funding and distribution experience via platforms such as Tumblbug.
07606
Reflections on Beauty and Culture
맹영한
This course explores the aesthetic traditions and artistic values of Korea, China, and Japan. Through the study of painting, architecture, crafts, literature, and visual culture, students will examine how different societies have understood and expressed beauty throughout history. Particular attention is given to key concepts such as harmony, nature, simplicity, emptiness, impermanence, and emotional sensitivity, which have shaped East Asian aesthetic thought.
The course encourages students to compare and critically analyze the aesthetic perspectives of the three cultures while exploring their influence on contemporary visual media, including film, animation, design, and digital content. By connecting traditional aesthetics with modern cultural practices, students will develop cultural literacy, critical thinking skills, and a deeper understanding of the diverse ways beauty is perceived and represented in East Asia.
07608
Brand Marketing
오윤지
This course is a project-based learning course designed to solve real-world brand marketing challenges faced by companies, grounded in a theoretical understanding of brand marketing. Students will learn fundamental marketing theories as well as key concepts and strategic case studies related to brand identity, positioning, consumer experience, and digital marketing. Based on this knowledge, they will analyze actual marketing challenges presented by participating companies and propose practical solutions. Throughout the project, students will receive mentoring from both the instructor and industry professionals, and the final outcomes will be evaluated and validated by practitioners. Through this process, students will develop both brand marketing strategy formulation skills and practical problem-solving capabilities.
07609
The Discovery of Scene
This course introduces the fundamental "language of film"—camera, composition, lighting, sound, and editing—through which a single scene creates meaning. Using familiar films and well-known scenes, it offers non-majors an accessible way to understand how directors convey meaning through the image and to cultivate a critical eye for reading film. Delivered as asynchronous online lectures with multilingual subtitles, the course allows learners to study at their own pace and lays the foundation for the offline practicum Project.
07610
Performance Design
서준
The <Performance Design> course explores the expansion of performance from traditional stage productions into multifaceted experiential spaces. Using visual design elements, signs, and metaphors, the course focuses on projecting the deep symbolic meanings and underlying narratives of a work into physical spaces.
At the beginning of the semester, students will engage in collaborative workshops encompassing planar(2D), spatial(3D), and spatiotemporal(4D) dimensions, thereby acquiring a profound understanding of physical structures and the significance of performance and design. Building upon this foundation, students will form multidisciplinary teams by integrating their individual expertise and artistic backgrounds(production, visual, sound, technology, etc.). These teams will proactively execute a complex, practical production process, ranging from concept ideation and narrative refinement to interdisciplinary integration and the final showcase. Through this comprehensive process, students will cultivate the collaborative competency required to successfully execute performance and design in a professional context.

07586
IoT Smart Home Design
This course aims to develop an understanding of IoT-based smart home environments and their application in spatial design. With the rapid expansion of intelligent environments such as smart homes, smart cities, and digital twins,spatial environments are evolving beyond mere physical structures into complex systems that integrate user data, sensor technologies, and automated systems. Accordingly, the importance of incorporating IoT technologies and user experience (UX) into spatial design has become increasingly significant.
In this course, students will learn the fundamental concepts of key technological components of smart homes, including IoT sensors, networks, and smart devices, and examine how these can be applied to spatial design. In addition, students will explore data-driven design approaches that analyze and optimize spaces based on user behavior and environmental data. Through this process, students will develop the ability to comprehensively understand and effectively integrate technology, space, and user experience into their design practice.
07518
Understanding Arts and Culture through OTT
김은혜
This course aims to recognize the increasing importance of arts and culture in our rapidly changing modern society, comprehensively understand the arts and cultural ecosystem, and explore the policies and legal frameworks that support it.
First, the course promotes understanding of the structure and operating principles of the arts and cultural ecosystem. It analyzes the value chain of arts and culture, from creation to distribution to consumption, and examines the roles and interactions of the actors involved at each stage. It also considers the impact of external factors such as technological advancements and social changes on the arts and cultural ecosystem. Through this, students develop the ability to understand the uniqueness and complexity of the arts and cultural field and to view phenomena from a holistic perspective.
Second, students learn about the process of formulating and implementing arts and cultural policies. They understand basic concepts such as the objectives, major areas, and formulation procedures of arts and cultural policies, and analyze major domestic and international policy cases. The course delves deeply into key issues in modern cultural policy, including the democratization of culture and cultural democracy, protection of cultural diversity, welfare of artists, and cultivation of cultural industries. In this process, students develop the ability to understand the impact of policies on the actual arts and cultural field and to explore desirable policy directions.
Third, students learn about the system and main contents of arts and culture-related laws and regulations. They understand the main contents of key regulations such as the Framework Act on Culture, Copyright Act, and Culture and Arts Promotion Act, and learn through case studies how these regulations are applied in the actual arts and cultural field. The course explores in depth the core legal values in the arts and cultural field, such as freedom of art and expression, protection of creators' rights, and the public nature of arts and culture. Through this, students develop legal thinking skills and the ability to respond to various legal issues in the arts and cultural field.
This course utilizes various practical learning methods in addition to theoretical learning. It provides opportunities for students to apply theory to real situations through guest lectures by field experts and case studies. It also fosters collaboration and communication skills through team projects, presentations, and discussions.
In particular, reflecting the educational philosophy of Catholic University, this course emphasizes developing ethical value judgment skills beyond simply conveying knowledge. By considering ways in which arts and culture can contribute to realizing individual dignity and social integration, and ways to care for socially disadvantaged groups and realize the common good through arts and culture, the course cultivates insight into creating a human-centered arts and cultural ecosystem.
Through this course, students will gain a comprehensive understanding of the arts and cultural ecosystem and develop skills such as policy analysis. Furthermore, they will cultivate creative and ethical leadership that can protect and spread the value of arts and culture in a rapidly changing environment. Based on this, after graduation, they will be able to grow into experts who can play a pivotal role in arts and culture-related public institutions, arts and cultural organizations, and cultural industry fields.

It will be very helpful for students to grow as professionals in this field if producers who specialize in non-script contents discuss and study non-script contents that is required by society and industry with students from an academic and practical perspective. The purpose of this course is to study and analyze all contents that does not require a structured script and to develop the ability to plan video content that can lead not only the Korean market but also global trends.

This learning experience will deepen students' understanding of the importance of data and the necessity of data-driven strategic decision-making.
Moreover, this course will cover the theoretical foundations of brand strategy, exploring key concepts such as brand equity, brand positioning, and brand identity in depth. Students will learn how to design effective brand strategies based on this theoretical knowledge, understanding the role and value of brands and learning how to strategically leverage these aspects during their learning process.
The formulation of brand strategies using data is a central focus of this course. Through this, students will develop the ability to integrate theory and practice, gaining a broad understanding of how data-driven strategies are applied across different industries. This integrative approach, combining theory and practical application, will equip students with the skills needed to implement data-driven brand management in their careers after graduation, enabling them to grow into competitive professionals in the marketing and branding fields in the digital age.

Keybord Harmony2
김지현
Keyboard harmony is a class that learns the harmony method, which is the basis of compositional music, through theory and practice, and develops the ability to understand the harmony that has been theoretically learned and to freely implement it on the keyboard. Along with basic knowledge of harmony, students learn improvisation that fills the harmony according to the number bass, the technique of filling the harmony according to the melody and completing the accompaniment in an appropriate pattern, modulation that changes the score to play the accompaniment instrument, and accompaniment method that fills the harmony according to the chord.
The teaching method is accompanied by one-on-one practice and feedback on the keyboard along with the theory class, and by practicing examples and other examples of the textbook, the theory can be applied to actual performance so that when playing, it can be played without difficulty.

07593
Fashion and Space as Art
This interdisciplinary theory course defines contemporary fashion not merely as clothing, but as a “contemporary visual culture and artistic discourse,” and analyzes it in depth through postmodern and contemporary art theories. It explores how fashion has absorbed artistic elements to expand its own aesthetic value, and how these outcomes are visualized within physical and conceptual spaces. By deconstructing and interpreting major fashion artworks and the aesthetic composition of the spaces surrounding them through the lens of art criticism, students will gain an understanding of the new aesthetic concepts created by the interaction of fashion, space, and art, and develop the critical eye necessary to interpret contemporary visual culture.

Drug delivery system
용석범
The Drug Delivery System (DDS) course provides an introduction to the principles and technologies used to improve the delivery and therapeutic efficacy of pharmaceutical agents in the body. This course covers the processes of drug absorption, distribution, metabolism, and excretion (ADME), and the design principles of various drug delivery carriers based on these pharmacokinetic properties. Students will learn the structure and function of advanced drug delivery platforms, including nanoparticles, lipid nanoparticles (LNPs), and polymer-based carriers. The course also explores targeted drug delivery, controlled release strategies, and the in vivo behavior of drug delivery systems. Through this course, students will acquire fundamental knowledge and practical insights into advanced drug delivery technologies applicable to a wide range of diseases and therapeutic development.

Advanced Technical Writing
Technical writing is an increasingly important skill in modern society, essential not only in the scientific and technological fields but across various industries. This course aims to provide students with advanced concepts and practical methods of technical writing, focusing on developing effective document creation and information delivery skills. In this advanced course, students will learn various skills necessary for writing technical documents and apply these skills to develop a deeper proficiency in technical writing. The main topics covered in the course are as follows:
1. The Need for and Importance of Technical Writing
 - The significance of technical documents in social and industrial contexts
 - What is a technical writer?
2. Fundamental Principles of Technical Writing
 - Principles of clarity, accuracy, and conciseness
3. Types of Technical Documents
 - Various types and structures of technical documents, such as reports, proposals, manuals, and research papers
4. Writing Strategies and Formats for Different Types of Technical Documents
 - Analysis and summarization of technical documents
 - Visual writing techniques
5. Technical Writing and Ethics
 - Principles of copyright and citation
6. Presentation and Feedback
 - Evaluation and feedback on students' written work

In this course, students study the design of Very Large Scale Integrated (VLSI) circuits. It is a course in digital design techniques using CMOS technology. Complementary Metal-Oxide Semiconductor (CMOS) technology and theory; CMOS circuit and logic design; layout rules and techniques; circuit characterization and performance estimation; CMOS subsystem design; VLSI systems design methods; VLSI Computer Aided Design (CAD) tools; laboratory experience in custom VLSI chip design on workstations using concepts of cell hierarchy; final project involving specification, design and evaluation of a VLSI chip or VLSI CAD program; and written report and oral presentation on the final project.

Philosophy
07558
East and West, The Philosophy of Traversal
신상희, 윤단비
This course will explore the cultural origins and differences between the two major worlds currently leading the global stage—East Asia and Europe—from a comparative philosophical perspective. Based on comparative philosophical inquiries, we examine how the encounter between East and West unfolded within the text of philosophy. Subsequently, we will consider how Eastern and Western cultures and philosophies meet in the modern world and how they should develop going forward.
07559
The Exchange of Civilizations, The Adventure of Thought
Memorizing the names of civilizations, learning their periods and locations, or studying their art and technology is meaningful work. However, this course goes beyond merely learning the content of each civilization. It will penetrate deeply into the rich stories contained within them, analyzing why and how these stories emerged and what impact they had on human life. Through exploring diverse civilizations that transcend time and space, students will come to realize that the core of civilization lies in human thought and understanding.
03842
Tradition of Western Philosophy
전석빈
Philosophy that deals with fundamental problems related to human life has formed the basis of every individual science. In this course, we consider the formation of western philosophy by focusing on the historical context in which important and influential philosophers were active; we study how philosophy has resolved problems in each era and how it has made important progress in each period. Students, based upon this, are expected to obtain a perspective through which they can observe our own problems (of the contemporary world) through a more fundamental and comprehensive view of the history of thought.
03844
Myth and Philosophy
김길수
Mythology that has been preserved in the histories of various people is not only a form of imagination, but sharply penetrates various aspects of human nature and explains them very clearly. In this course we analyze various types of humans and the events we see in mythology, and critically observe them. As we can often see in psychology and literature, a close analysis of events implicitly described in mythology can provide us with a way of understanding and gaining profound reflections on human culture that can be expressed in philosophical language.

03501
Psychological Phenomena and Emotions
신상희
The human is not only a thinking animal, but also emotional one. Humans can be angry, depressed, regretful, or can also rejoice, be delighted, or be pleased. Our internal psychology is characterized as an endless influx and extinction of these emotions. What is the nature of emotion? What is its origin? And how is it different or related to thought that is an operation of reason? In this course, philosophical answers to these questions will be explored through various approaches.

07458
Developing into an Attractive Professional
유희
The course “Developing into an Attractive Professional” is designed to help students develop a strong and positive self-identity through self-understanding, while systematically enhancing key soft skills required in today’s society—including self-expression, communication, empathy, teamwork, and leadership. It is a career competency development course aimed at preparing students for successful social integration and future employment.
The primary goals of the course are to: Enhance students’ self-awareness and self-expression, Strengthen personal branding and communication skills, Develop core social soft skills such as empathy, teamwork, and leadership, Improve students’ confidence and adaptability through experience-based activities.
To achieve these objectives, the course incorporates: Psychological diagnostic tools (such as Transactional Analysis and API profiling), Group activities and role-playing exercises, Feedback-driven sessions, The creation of a self-development portfolio.
Through this course, students will: Discover and develop their unique personal strengths and value, Improve their self-efficacy and interpersonal competence, Strengthen their ability to adapt to organizational life, Build essential career readiness skills, including confidence in job interviews and workplace communication.
This course not only supports individual student growth but also lays a solid foundation for a successful transition into society and the workforce.
07459
Strategic Interview Image for Career Success
This course is designed for students who are actively engaged in job search activities, including employment, internships, and field training. It is a practical, hands-on course aimed at strengthening students’ abilities to formulate strategies appropriate to various interview formats and to enhance self-presentation skills such as public speaking and image-making.
As interview formats have diversified—ranging from discussion-based and presentation (PT) interviews to AI-based assessments—the importance of practical interview competency is growing. To respond to these trends, students must develop the ability to effectively express their job-fit and organizational-fit through structured interview preparation, hands-on exercises, and feedback-centered instruction.
Accordingly, the course aims to: Analyze current interview trends and build strategies tailored to each format, Improve the ability to organize self-introduction and experience-based speech, Train students in non-verbal communication and image-making for interviews, Enhance practical interview skills through mock interviews and simulations
The curriculum includes: First impressions and image-making, Structuring self-introductions, Responding effectively to interview questions, Non-verbal communication such as facial expressions, tone of voice, posture, Self-expression strategies and practical skills specific to each interview type.
Students will also benefit from mock interview sessions, peer and instructor feedback, and video-based self-assessment, maximizing learning outcomes.
Through this course, students are expected to build interview confidence and practical readiness, ultimately leading to improved job search outcomes. Additionally, the course addresses the core employment competencies sought by industry, contributing to better alignment between university education and workforce expectations.

  - Help increase the chances of getting the right job with a well developed job search strategy

07052
Job Change and Industry Trend
99
The subject of 'Job Changes and Industry Trend' is a subject to learn about changing business management and new jobs(occupations). The 4th Industrial Revolution and Corona 19 changed corporate management and new jobs were created.
When students set their career path, they often do not know about various jobs and company information. At this time, it is difficult to set a specific career plan. About 7 million domestic companies (KOSTAT, as of 2021) are steadily emerging and disappearing. The 4th Industrial Revolution and the corona virus are causing major changes in corporate production methods, investment, and supply chains. Students learn how to find the right company and job information among numerous companies. And to help design specific employment goals and systematic university life. Through this subject, the goal of 'a university that finds me' is achieved.
06452
Job information analysis and job strategy establishment
조재한
The subject of job information analysis and job strategy establishment will cover practical and strategic ways to prepare for employment for third and fourth graders. In particular, in order to adapt to changes in the environment of industry and business and to successfully get a job by taking advantage of their major, students will organize their thoughts on the job and explore various employment cases in the same major and similar situations. Through this, you can objectively analyze your situation and interests and establish realistic employment goals. After setting goals for employment, we learn about various channels and effective ways to use them, such as job sites and employment-related communities. In addition, data such as acceptance letters and job interviews that suit students' employment goals will be analyzed to derive key information needed to fill out job applications, and in fact, a standard plan for job applications that can be used by individual students in future employment activities will be drawn up. The completed job application form will not only be one-time, but will be updated from time to time with the development of students' own competencies and changes in industry and business through the course. This course will be a time to use the class to prepare essentials for actual employment activities, and it will be a class where students with similar or diverse majors can get rid of vague preparation for employment and increase their effectiveness in employment.

06566
Key employment strategies
This specialization will help you develop the Korean language strategies and communication skills you need to advance in your professional career.  Whether you already have a successful career and are looking to move forward, whether you’re looking to change careers, whether you’re starting out in the world of work, or whether you’re coming back into the world of work after some time away – if you believe in working for more than a paycheck, then this specialization will help you. The core courses cover preparing for a successful job search, including self research and research of the job market and industries of interest; strengthening your interview skills by recognizing what hiring managers are looking for and taking steps to prepare for the types of tough questions today's premier companies use; and preparing a resume, cover letter and supporting business documents. The capstone will allow you to apply the skills you learn in this specialization to your own job search.
A key benefit of this specialization is the opportunities you'll have to practice your interviewing skills with other job-seekers from around the world. You’ll give them feedback and they’ll give you feedback. In this process, you’ll gain new insight into what makes a speaker successful and you’ll gain confidence in your interviewing skills.
This course, Job Success: Get Hired or Promoted in Three Steps, will prepare you to stand out in a crowded applicant pool so that you can get hired or promoted. In three steps you will leave this course with 

1. An upgraded social media presence (one that you can be proud of)
2. A visual, infographic resume that will get you noticed
3. A professional pitch that highlights your strengths and skills

When creating this course, we listened to potential employers, took the advice of recruiters, conducted informal research on best practices and we drew from our own experiences as professionals who have sought out and hired quality candidates.
The goal of hiring managers is not just to hire people who need a job. It’s to hire people who believe in their organization, its mission and the work that’s involved in the job position. Every hiring manager knows: Hire people to do a job and they’ll work for your money. Hire people who believe in the work and they’ll work for their passion.

06175
Life and Career Design
In this course, 'Life and Career Design' you will learn how to think strategically and professionally about career self-management and design. Through this course, you will learn how to design and make the best of your college life. You will study about three important perspectives on career choices.

The three are job interests, job values, and job competency.
You will be able to:
- Learn how to manage your career in college. In particular, you will learn how to utilize various career management systems at The Catholic University of Korea.
- You will learn how to navigate yourself. We will study the theory of career choice, including topics such as transferable skills, job interests, job values, and job competencies.
- You will also learn about the different jobs of the company in line with the changing of careers. You can make your dream a reality by learning about the duties related to R&D, production management, quality control, personnel, marketing, and finance.
- Finally, you will learn how to use external activities during your college life. This course will introduce activities that will help to develop your career, such as contests, internships, volunteer activities, and part-time jobs.

03157
Automata Theory
This course will cover the Chomsky hierarchy of Formal Languages (regular sets, context-free languages, context-sensitive languages, and recursively enumerable languages) and the types of grammars and automata associated with each class in the hierarchy. Critical Reading Across the Disciplines
56
This lecture focuses on providing useful techniques and skills that are highly relevant to students’ academic success in college as well as their lives after college. More precisely, this course covers overall general skills in critical reading ranging from previewing to careful reading techniques and also the ones that are highly related to information searching. Additionally, the training of these reading techniques will be conducted mainly utilizing the English language to enhance students’ ability in dealing with English-texts. Considering the diverse backgrounds and majors of students, this class utilizes texts from various disciplines and topics. After taking this class, students will be able to process, acquire, and organize information efficiently and critically while reading not only academic texts but also other ones.

Topics include Cyber law, Digital privacy, Cyber bullying, Cyber defamation, Cyber sexual harrassment, and the role of media in shaping public perception of cyber crime. 06795
Global Business and Legal Issues
In this course, students will examine various global businesses like Apple, Microsoft, Google, Samsung, etc and learn to develop an awareness of legal consequences that emerge from such business practices, specifically on the impact of intellectual property(“IP”) and its legal obligations. For those who are interested in working for the international companies, this course provides an overview of various IP issues, that may frequently arise in the field through the lenses of contracts, trademarks, trade dress, and trade secrets. Students will learn different types of IP, purpose and functions of IP, registration & acquisition process, and infringement & preservation of such rights.

06819
Global Health from Multidisciplinary Perspectives
김민우
The course will introduce students to the main concepts of the global health field and enhance their understandings in the social, economic, cultural, legal, and political processes by which global health policy influences global health objectives. Students will be able to discuss the social, political and economic determinants of global health and identify the evolving national institutions, international organizations, private interests, and global partnerships structuring global health policy. Students will further analyze the ethical, moral and legal norms that frame global health governance and evaluate global health policy to address disease prevention and health promotion. Potential topics to be explored include basic research methods in global health, health systems and management, infectious diseases and epidemics, global nutrition and agriculture, child health, sexual and reproductive health, humanitarian aid, environmental health, conflict, culture, and gender, etc.
